title: Maintaining consistency in terminology: a guide for technical writers on Mac
metaTitle: Maintaining consistency in terminology for technical documentation on Mac
description: Learn how to perform a terminology audit on Mac to ensure your documentation remains accurate and consistent, reducing user confusion and support costs.
intro: Maintaining consistency in terminology is the process of ensuring that every feature, button, and concept in your documentation uses the same name throughout your content. Without a formal audit, your documentation quickly becomes a collection of conflicting terms that frustrate users and drive up support volume.
tldr: Inconsistent terminology acts as a hidden tax on your users.
A terminology audit identifies and fixes naming conflicts.
You can maintain consistency using free tools like Vale or a simple glossary.
Lazur helps you audit faster by pointing at inconsistencies on your screen.

blocks.text: Why terminology audits are necessary for technical writers

Terminology drift happens naturally as products evolve. A feature might start as a 'Network connector' in early designs, become an 'Ethernet port' in the manual, and end up as a 'LAN port' in the UI. When you fail at maintaining consistency in terminology, you force the user to guess which term is correct. This uncertainty leads to support tickets where the user describes a feature using a term you never documented.
The hidden cost of inconsistent language

Poor terminology impacts your bottom line. It creates a cognitive load that slows down onboarding. If a user spends extra time trying to match your text to the screen, they are less likely to finish the task. In regulated industries, this is not just a nuisance. It is a compliance risk. Using the wrong term for a safety switch or a medical setting can lead to real world errors.
How to perform a terminology audit

items: Create a master glossary in a single file like terminology.adoc or a shared spreadsheet.
Scan your current documentation for synonyms of key features.
Identify the 'source of truth' for each term by checking the UI or talking to developers.
Replace all variations with the approved term across your entire library.
Add the new term to your style guide to prevent future drift.

blocks.text: You do not need expensive software to fix this. Vale is a powerful open source linter. You can configure it to flag forbidden words in your Markdown files. If you use a simple text editor like iA Writer or Obsidian, Vale runs in the background and highlights issues as you type. This keeps your terminology clean without changing your workflow.

faq.question: How often should I perform a terminology audit?
faq.answer: Perform a major audit every six months or after a significant product release. Smaller, incremental checks should happen during every sprint.

faq.question: Can AI help with terminology audits?
faq.answer: AI is great at spotting patterns, but it often struggles with domain-specific naming. Always verify AI suggestions against your official glossary.

causes.title: Lack of a central glossary
causes.text: Different team members use their own preferred terms without a shared reference.

causes.title: Rapid product changes
causes.text: The UI updates faster than the documentation, leaving old terms behind.

fixes.title: Create a living glossary
fixes.text: Maintain a simple document that lists every approved term and what it refers to.

fixes.title: Use automated linters
fixes.text: Set up Vale to automatically flag inconsistent terms in your text files.
